diagnosis.summary: Nightly ingest for 2026-10-01 failed because the orders.csv landing file is truncated mid-row. It stops at line 266 with 3 of 7 fields and has 265 rows, against 461 the day before. The header is unchanged. I proposed requesting upstream redelivery of orders for 2026-10-01, then rerunning.

root_cause.explanation: The upstream export of orders for 2026-10-01 was interrupted. The file is cut off mid-row (line 266: '13666,952,2'), has no trailing newline, and ends at order_id 13666. order_items and payments reference order_ids up to 13841, so rows are missing. Strict CSV parsing then fails the ingest step.

evidence.claim: Ingest failed on raw.orders with a CSV column-count error at line 266 (3 columns found, 7 expected)
The orders file is truncated mid-row with the header intact, and has 265 rows against 461 the previous day
The other 10-01 tables are complete, and order_items and payments reference orders past the truncation point
The runbook says a truncated file is a one-off delivery glitch to be fixed by redelivery, not by editing the file or changing the schema

alternatives_considered: Schema change (renamed, added or type-changed column): ruled out because the header matches the contract and the error is a parse error, not a schema mismatch or cast error
Ignore errors or null padding on ingest: rejected because it would load a partial orders table and hide about 40% missing data
Truncate the file to the last good row or hand-edit it: rejected because the runbook forbids it and the missing orders would be lost
rerun_only: rejected because the same truncated file would fail again
Escalate to upstream_app_team: kept as the fallback if redelivery returns the same broken file

proposal.rationale: The orders landing file for 2026-10-01 is truncated mid-row. The header matches the contract. A partial export is a one-off delivery problem, and the runbook maps it to redelivery. Relaxing the parser would silently drop the missing orders.
